title: Social Security Act 1991
converter: cth_convert_sym.py (a copy of docx_text() and the volume joining of the workbench converter tools/fetch/fetch-source.py that also maps Symbol-font and private-use characters; kept outside the repository); the first deposit used tools/fetch/fetch-source.py
text_caveat: The version in force from 2026-09-20 has no registered compilation yet; this text is the latest compilation (No. 232, in force from 2026-07-01), so amendments commencing on or after that date may be missing.

reconverted_2026_11_07.previous_converter: tools/fetch/fetch-source.py (docx_text), the converter of the 2026-09-22 deposit
reconverted_2026_11_07.source_docx_note: the six Word volumes C2026C00336VOL01-VOL06, joined in order; same compilation as the first deposit
reconverted_2026_11_07.why: docx_text() dropped every Word <w:sym> character, which is how the Register writes some characters in the Symbol and Wingdings fonts, and kept Symbol-font characters typed as text as raw private-use code points (U+F0xx), which display as empty boxes. cth_convert_sym.py maps them to Unicode (Symbol F0D7 ·, F0B4 ×, F02D −, F0B7 •, F0A3 ≤, F0B3 ≥ and the like) and Wingdings boxes to "[ ]".
reconverted_2026_11_07.what_changed: Two things. (1) One multiplication sign restored: Symbol F0B4 × had been dropped from the s 1061ED(4) example (line 12313), which read "6% $4680 = $280.80" and now reads "6% × $4680 = $280.80"; C2004A04121.formulas.md already gave the restored paragraph. (2) 7 Symbol-font bullets kept as U+F0B7 (empty boxes) in the s 92A simplified outline of the pension bonus scheme (lines 4337-4343) are written as "•". No other w:sym character or private-use code point is in the Word volumes. Reconverted from the same Word volumes (same download sha256); a diff against the first deposit shows no other change (same 51,635 lines; 2 characters added, the × and its space).
reconverted_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: none: baseline-2026-10, baseline-2026-11 and naive-2026-10 rely on neither changed line (the s 1061ED(4) example and the s 92A outline are not encoded, and no rule, case or finding cites them)
